 Local News Nicobar Great Nicobar Consumers Charged ₹1,229.92 Extra Per 19 Kg Commercial LPG Cylinder for Transportation
 Last updated: October 26, 2026 8:29 pm 
 Tarun Karthick 
 Share 
 4 Min Read 
 SHARE 
 Campbell Bay | October 26, 2026 
 Commercial LPG consumers in Great Nicobar Island are being charged an additional ₹1,229.92 per 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder towards transportation, taking the price of a cylinder to ₹4,541.42, compared to ₹3,311.50 in Sri Vijaya Puram.
 The Consumers Co-operative Stores Ltd. (CCS), the sole LPG distributor in Great Nicobar Island, has been levying the additional transportation charges on commercial LPG consumers. The steep increase has placed an additional financial burden on businesses in the southernmost island of the Andaman and Nicobar archipelago, prompting consumers to seek the intervention of the authorities.
 In early October 2026, when commercial LPG cylinders were transported to Great Nicobar and made available to consumers, they were surprised by the price charged by the distributor. Upon enquiring with the distributor’s staff at Campbell Bay, consumers were informed that ₹1,229.92 was being charged over and above the cost of the cylinder towards transportation.
 When Nicobar Times sought clarification from CCS authorities, it was informed that the charges incurred in the actual transportation of LPG cylinders were being recovered from consumers.
 A breakup of the transportation costs provided to Nicobar Times showed that the amount includes expenses for transporting filled commercial LPG cylinders from Sri Vijaya Puram to Campbell Bay and returning empty cylinders from Campbell Bay to Sri Vijaya Puram.
 The charges include truck transportation, labour, handling and stevedoring, PMB charges, freight, GST on freight, labour for unloading and truck charges upon discharge. According to the breakup provided, these expenses are charged for both the onward transportation of filled cylinders and the return transportation of empty cylinders.
 Earlier, CCS charged ₹510.15 per 19 kg commercial LPG cylinder towards transportation. The charge has now increased to ₹1,229.92, more than doubling the earlier amount.
 The issue has added to the concerns of commercial LPG consumers in Great Nicobar, an island that has also faced LPG supply disruptions. Both commercial and domestic LPG cylinders remained unavailable for a prolonged period during a recent supply crisis.
 The additional transportation costs have become a significant burden for commercial consumers, who are seeking the Administration’s intervention to address the issue and ensure that a fair transportation cost is fixed for commercial LPG cylinders supplied to the island.
 The development comes as the Government of India is implementing the Great Nicobar Island Project, a major initiative comprising a transshipment port, a greenfield international airport, a township and a power plant.
 Nicobar Times also contacted officials of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) for their comments. The official informed the publication that the grievance was being forwarded to the concerned LPG Wing officials. However, no further response had been received from the corporation until the time of filing this report.
 Commercial LPG consumers in Great Nicobar have urged the authorities to examine the additional charges and take appropriate action to ensure that the transportation cost component does not impose an excessive financial burden on them.
